questions.stem: Concerning viruses and archaea (one or more correct answers):
options: Viruses are non-obligate parasites with their own metabolism
Archaea are very similar to bacteria morphologically and metabolically
Viruses have a cytoplasm and a true nucleus
Archaea have rRNAs similar to those of eukaryotes

questions.stem: About detoxification in the hepatocyte:
options: Cytochrome P450 is an enzyme of the SER membrane whose active site is on the luminal side of the SER
P450 action hydroxylates the drug, increasing its water solubility
The hydroxylated drug is translocated to the cytosol
In the SER lumen, the hydroxylated drug undergoes glucuronidation, which increases its solubility

questions.stem: About protein glycosylation in the rough endoplasmic reticulum:
options: The preformed oligosaccharide motif (2 GlcNAc, 9 Man, 3 Glc) is transferred from dolichol-phosphate to an N-glycosylation consensus sequence containing serine or threonine
The oligosaccharide motifs (2 GlcNAc, 9 Man, 3 Glc) are only modified after the glycoprotein is transferred to the Golgi apparatus
N-glycosylation takes place in the RER lumen during translation
O-glycosylation indicates the extent of protein folding so that proteins only leave the ER once correctly folded
questions.explanation: The N-glycosylation consensus sequence contains asparagine (Asn-X-Ser/Thr).

questions.stem: Ribosomes bound to the ER membrane make membrane proteins destined for the membrane of:
options: The endoplasmic reticulum
Peroxisomes
The plasma membrane
Lysosomes

questions.stem: The Golgi apparatus:
options: Sorts molecules before their cellular or extracellular distribution, notably by adding addressing signals
Takes part, via Golgi vesicles, in renewing the glycocalyx
Takes part in the post-translational maturation of proteins
Plays a role in incorporating sulfates into glycoproteins

questions.stem: Concerning viruses:
options: Viruses use the ribosomes of the cells they infect to synthesize their proteins
Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria
Some viruses are surrounded by an envelope formed when they cross cell membranes
They can only reproduce by infecting a host cell

questions.stem: Concerning the biochemical modifications seen in the Golgi apparatus:
options: Maturations in the Golgi system are finished before arrival at the TGN, which handles specific addressing of molecules and formation of coated vesicles
Modifications of the N-linked motif in the Golgi determine the addressing of the protein to a given compartment
Sulfotransferases in the trans-Golgi allow sulfation of some glycoproteins
N-glycosylated proteins can undergo deglycosylations followed by additional glycosylations

questions.stem: Concerning bacteria:
options: No bacterium can be beneficial to humans
Gram-positive bacteria have thick cell walls
Bacteria may have a capsule of lipid nature
Bacteria always contain a plasma membrane

questions.stem: Concerning transport across the plasma membrane:
options: Passive membrane transport via a permease can be blocked by competitive inhibitors
Raft endocytosis leads to the formation of caveolae whose membrane is rich in protein domains
Regulated (controlled) exocytosis is a continuous process that consumes energy
Simple diffusion across the plasma membrane involves specific recognition between an extracellular messenger and a surface receptor

questions.stem: Coatomers are proteins involved in:
options: Retrograde transport
Anterograde transport
Endocytosis
Exocytosis

questions.stem: Concerning the plasma membrane:
options: The cell coat plays a role in recognition, cell adhesion and physical protection of the cell
Plasma membrane proteins can cross the membrane several times
The plasma membrane is a complex dynamic structure in constant motion, passing through different states of structural organization depending on physiological activity
Phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine are found mainly in the outer leaflet

questions.stem: Concerning transmembrane exchanges:
options: Simple diffusion occurs without energy expenditure thanks to a passive permease
Unlike lipids, which are mobile, proteins have no mobility within the membrane
Facilitated diffusions are symports
Aquaporins are multi-pass integral proteins that allow water to cross the membrane

questions.stem: The plasma membrane is called a "fluid mosaic" because:
options: It is rigid and fixed
It is made of a fluid lipid bilayer with mobile proteins
It consists only of proteins
It allows no movement of its components

questions.stem: Concerning protein synthesis:
options: Protein synthesis always starts at the RER
Protein synthesis requires tRNAs that match a given amino acid to each anticodon of the mRNA
Translation ends when the ribosome reaches the stop codon of the mRNA
The RER picks up certain specific proteins from the cytosol as soon as they are synthesized

questions.stem: Archaea:
options: Are found everywhere in the environment, including the human body
Are used to produce heat-resistant enzymes
Have rRNAs different from those of eubacteria and eukaryotes
Are more similar to bacteria than to eukaryotes at the molecular level

questions.stem: Concerning eukaryotic ribosomes:
options: They are not bounded by a membrane
They are complexes of rRNA and ribosomal proteins
They catalyze DNA replication
They can be free in the cytosol or bound to the ER membrane and to the outer membrane of the nuclear envelope

questions.stem: Concerning membrane functions:
options: In exocytosis, the cell takes in macromolecules by forming new vesicles at the plasma membrane
Macromolecules and particles cross the plasma membrane by passive phenomena
Receptor-mediated endocytosis lets the cell take up specific substances via clathrin-coated pits
In pinocytosis, a portion of the plasma membrane invaginates to internalize a fraction of the intracellular medium

questions.stem: During rRNA maturation and ribosome formation there is:
options: Synthesis of a 45S pre-mRNA molecule
Incorporation of 18S rRNA into the large ribosomal subunits
Synthesis of a 5S rRNA molecule outside the nucleolus
Association of ribosomal proteins with mRNAs before these molecules leave the nucleus

questions.stem: Protein translocation into the ER involves the SRP complex; this complex is:
options: A ribonucleoprotein complex
A translocation channel, also called the translocon
A protease cleaving the signal sequence
A signal sequence allowing translocation into the ER

questions.stem: Among the conformational and chemical modifications of a protein in the RER, there is:
options: Folding by BiP proteins
Sulfation by sulfotransferases
Degradation in the proteasome
N-glycosylation and O-glycosylation by glycosyltransferases

questions.stem: About protein folding in the RER:
options: Folding gives the three-dimensional conformation needed for their function
Folding depends on the KDEL sequence, which helps and controls folding
After synthesis in the RER, misfolded proteins are sent by vesicles to lysosomes for degradation
Protein misfolding in the RER causes protein synthesis to stop and the cell to undergo apoptosis

questions.stem: Fate of proteins:
options: Misfolded proteins in the ER lumen must be translocated to the cytosol and possibly deglycosylated before proteolysis in a proteasome
The proteasome is a cytosolic system for degrading ubiquitinated proteins
Ubiquitin is a protein that tags other proteins destined for degradation
Proteins synthesized in the ER, whether membrane or soluble, can undergo maturations

questions.stem: Concerning retrograde vesicular transport:
options: It occurs either from the Golgi to the cell membrane or from the Golgi to the mitochondrion
This transport notably returns non-resident proteins of the RER
Transmembrane proteins resident in the RER have a KDEL signal allowing their return to their compartment
The CGN emits COP II vesicles that fuse with the RER
questions.explanation: Official key: D. (Note: retrograde CGN → ER vesicles are normally COP I; KDEL is the signal of soluble ER-resident proteins, KKXX that of transmembrane ones.)

questions.stem: Concerning the Golgi apparatus:
options: O-glycosylation occurs on serine and threonine residues of the protein
In the medial and trans saccules of the Golgi, glycosyltransferases add new sugars
It is involved in modifying, sorting and dispatching proteins and lipids
Post-Golgi compartments of the endomembrane system include lysosomes, peroxisomes and secretory vesicles

questions.stem: The Golgi apparatus is a site of:
options: Maturation and chemical tagging of proteins
Polyubiquitination of misfolded proteins
Modification of the N-linked oligosaccharides of glycoproteins
Proteolysis of proteins that misfolded in the RER

questions.stem: You are doing a five-year basic research project on the migration of breast cancer cells, a key phenomenon in metastasis. You prepare a cell line from a malignant breast tumor. What protocol gives this line?
options: Biopsy + primary culture
Biopsy + primary culture + flow cytometry sorting
Biopsy + primary culture + flow cytometry sorting + immortalization by lentiviral transfection
Biopsy + primary culture + immortalization by lentiviral transfection
questions.explanation: Tumor cells are already immortal; sorting isolates the tumor cells.

questions.stem: On the cell line obtained, you want to assess the expression of integrin α1β2, a membrane protein involved in cell migration. You have a simple primary antibody and a fluorochrome-coupled secondary antibody. Which technique will you use?
options: Cell fractionation
Direct fluorescent immunolabeling
Indirect fluorescent immunolabeling
Pulse-chase technique

questions.stem: How can you analyze the results of the technique used to assess integrin α1β2 expression?
options: With the confocal fluorescence microscope
With the fluorescence microscope
With the inverted phase-contrast microscope
With flow cytometry

questions.stem: The next step is to study the migration kinetics of your cell line by measuring cell speed on different matrices. Which laboratory tool should you use?
options: Flow cytometry
Scanning electron microscopy
Transmission electron microscopy
Light microscopy

questions.stem: In your cell line you want to study the ultrastructure of raft domains involved in cell migration. You do a cell fractionation to isolate the plasma membrane. Which protocol yields a large quantity of plasma membrane from your cell line?
options: Homogenization followed by differential ultracentrifugation (DUC)
Homogenization followed by gradient ultracentrifugation (GUC)
Fluorescent immunolabeling followed by homogenization and gradient ultracentrifugation (GUC)
Homogenization followed by differential ultracentrifugation (DUC) then gradient ultracentrifugation (GUC)
